Dictionaries are one of Python’s best features; they are the building blocks of many efficient and elegant algo- rithms. 11.1 A dictionary is a mapping A dictionary is like a list, but more general. In a list, the indices have to be integers; in a dictionary they can be (almost) any type. A dictionary contains a collection of indices, which are called keys, and a collection of values. Each key is associated with a single value. The association of a key and a value is called a key-value pair or sometimes an item. In mathematical language, a dictionary represents a mapping from keys to values, so you can also say that each key “maps to” a value.
